decisions.category: safe-area env() with validated closed-scale fallback
decisions.evidence: line 3599: the scanner emits this extension-boundary only AFTER validating the fallback term (spacing.mjs::analyzeEnvironmentSpacing runs analyzeSpacingTerm on it and reports a boundary only when that produced no finding), so var(--space-0) is a registered scale value. The inset itself is device-reported at runtime and cannot be on any closed scale, which is why the rule is a boundary rather than debt.

decisions.category: root font-size clamp() bounded by registered tokens
decisions.evidence: line 150: every bound in the clamp() is a registered token; the only non-token leaf is --user-font-size, the runtime user font-size preference written by ProfileSection.tsx -- a founder-approved permanent non-token category. typography.mjs reclassifies this to extension-boundary (not a silent pass) only when every OTHER leaf is a registered token, mirroring the safe-area env() carve-out; a clamp() with a raw pixel bound still reports.

decisions.category: tree-indent runtime depth multiplied by registered tokens
decisions.evidence: line 129 (anchored on `calc(var(--space-2-5)`): the custom property (or template interpolation) holds a UNITLESS nesting depth, and every dimensional term is a registered spacing token. spacing.mjs::combineCalc emits this boundary only when the unregistered value is multiplied directly against a value traced to a registered token (isTrustedTokenPx, set only by the token lookup, never by a literal). A per-row depth count can never itself be a registered token because its value varies per row. Adversarially tested: a raw pixel term, an unregistered dimensional token, chained multiplies and division all still block.
